curriculum.title: Creation, Order, and the Image of God

core.big_idea: Creation establishes God's sovereignty and humanity's dignity, vocation, and creaturely limits.

passages.reading_note: Track structure, divine speech, goodness, image, blessing, and vocation.
Observe wonder, creaturely smallness, honour, and delegated rule.
Use to clarify vocation and creaturely limits.

core.metanarrative_position: Creation and rule: God orders a good world and appoints image-bearing humans to responsible, bounded vocation.

claims.statement: Genesis 1 presents God as sovereign Creator whose speech orders the world and declares it good.
Humanity-male and female-is made in God’s image and given a vocation within creation.
Psalm 8 holds together human smallness within the cosmos and God-given honour and responsibility.
The image of God grounds equal human dignity without reducing worth to intelligence, independence, productivity, ethnicity, sex, or ability.
This curriculum does not make one chronology or creation mechanism a salvation or fellowship test.
claims.credible_alternative: Young-earth, old-earth, literary-framework, and evolutionary-creation readings differ over chronology, genre, and mechanism.
claims.interpretive_hinge: How literary structure, Hebrew terms, ancient context, scientific evidence, and canonical theology relate.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present a scientific model as though it were a direct quotation from Genesis or question salvation on that basis.

core.interpretation_skill: Compare narrative and poetry; distinguish theological claims from chronology and mechanism models.

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse Genesis 1 and Psalm 8 and explain the relationship between God’s sovereignty, human dignity, and human vocation.
learning.extension_objective: Evaluate a creation claim by separating explicit text, canonical synthesis, scientific model, and prudential application.
know: God creates and orders the world.
Humans are made in God’s image.
understand: Dignity is received from God, not earned through capacity or achievement.
Creaturely limits are part of faithful humanity, not a defect to overcome.
practise: Treat one overlooked person with image-bearing dignity.
Practise one bounded act of stewardship rather than fantasies of total control.
become: A student who worships the Creator, honours people, and accepts responsible limits.
success_evidence: The student distinguishes dignity from function.
The student compares Genesis 1 and Psalm 8 by genre.
The student labels a chronology claim as model rather than explicit text.

zero_prep_card.objective: Students explain how creation establishes God’s sovereignty, human dignity, vocation, and limits.
zero_prep_card.opening: Ask: Is human worth something we earn, measure, or receive? List common modern answers before reading.
say: Genesis begins with God as Creator and ruler.
Male and female humans bear God’s image and receive responsibility.
Psalm 8 combines humility before the cosmos with astonishing God-given honour.
Theological claims about Creator and image must be distinguished from disputed chronology and mechanism models.
ask: What is said of all humanity in Genesis 1:26-28?
What tension does Psalm 8 hold together?
What vocation and limits appear in Genesis 2?
Which claims are explicit text and which belong to later models?
zero_prep_card.do: Complete the Creation Claim Audit and label each statement Text, Synthesis, Model, or Application.
zero_prep_card.close: Pray for worship, equal regard for people, responsible work, and humility about limits.

preparation.passage_context: Genesis 1 is a highly structured creation account culminating in humanity and divine rest; Psalm 8 is worshipful poetry reflecting on human place and vocation. Genesis 2 supplies a complementary garden-scale scene.
text_observations: Divine speech and evaluation structure Genesis 1.
Image language is applied to male and female humanity before any achievement.
Psalm 8 moves from cosmic scale to human honour and delegated dominion.
interpretation_notes: Do not assume “image” is exhausted by one faculty such as rationality.
Dominion must be read under God’s ownership and the garden task of serving/keeping, not as licence for exploitation.
Discuss creation models only with accurate labels and charitable representation.
theological_guardrails: Do not rank human dignity by ability, development, disability, productivity, ethnicity, or sex.
Do not make one scientific model a test of salvation or fidelity.
Do not make environmental stewardship into either political party loyalty or nature worship.

likely_questions.question: What exactly is the image of God?
likely_questions.purpose: Present major proposals as partial dimensions-representation, relationship, vocation, moral/spiritual capacity-without reducing dignity to one capacity.

likely_questions.question: Does Genesis require six twenty-four-hour days?
likely_questions.purpose: State the project’s non-salvific position and explain that genre, language, sequence, and scientific models require fuller study.

discussion_questions.question: What is given to humanity before any achievement?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Explain implications for disability and status.

discussion_questions.question: How does Psalm 8 combine humility and honour?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: Humans are small yet crowned with honour.

discussion_questions.question: What is the difference between dominion and domination?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: Responsible rule under God versus exploitative control.

discussion_questions.question: Which creation claims require evidence beyond the explicit words of Genesis?

activities.title: Creation Claim Audit
steps: Label Text, Synthesis, Model, or Application.
activities.learning_link: Prevents conflating theology, exegesis, science, and policy.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Audit four claims on the board.

activities.title: Dignity Without Ranking
steps: Read descriptions varying age, ability, status, and achievement.
activities.learning_link: Tests whether image-of-God language actually resists performance-based worth.

closing.prayer_prompt: Worship the Creator and ask for humble, responsible, equal regard for people.
closing.take_home_line: Our dignity is received from God; our vocation is responsible; our power remains creaturely and limited.

family.title: Worth We Receive
family.parent_intro: This study asks what grounds human worth and how image-bearing responsibility should shape family life.

flow.instructions: Use the opening prompt to connect the lesson to ordinary family life.
Ask what humans receive from God and what responsibility follows.
Sort statements into Worth Received, Responsibility Given, or Model Debated.
Choose the weekly action, then pray together.

questions: Why can no person’s dignity depend on intelligence or achievement?
What is one form of responsible dominion in our home?

interactive.title: Worth, Work, or Model?
interactive.instructions: Sort claims into received dignity, assigned vocation, and disputed creation model.

family.weekly_action: Choose one person often overlooked and show concrete respect or service this week.
family.prayer: Creator God, teach us to honour every person, care for Your world, and accept our limits with humility.
family.parent_note: Keep creation-model debate separate from judgments about another person’s salvation.

quiz.question: Who bears God’s image in Genesis 1?
quiz.explanation: The image claim precedes achievement and applies broadly.

quiz.question: What does Psalm 8 hold together?
quiz.explanation: The psalm joins humility with vocation.

quiz.question: A person’s image-bearing worth depends on intelligence and productivity.
quiz.explanation: Dignity is received from God rather than earned.

quiz.question: How should creation chronology be classified in this curriculum?
options: A debated interpretive model, not a salvation test
A subject Scripture never touches at all

answer.text: A debated interpretive model, not a salvation test

quiz.explanation: The project affirms core creation theology while allowing model comparison.

puzzle.title: Text, Synthesis, Model, Application
puzzle.instructions: Sort each claim by evidence class.
items: Humans are made in God’s image.
Human dignity must not be ranked by ability.
Genesis requires one specific modern scientific model.

groups.label: Explicit text
items: Humans are made in God’s image.

groups.label: Canonical synthesis
items: Human dignity must not be ranked by ability.

groups.label: Model claim
items: Genesis requires one specific modern scientific model.

printables.title: Creation Claim Audit
printables.purpose: Distinguish explicit creation theology, canonical synthesis, scientific or chronological models, and practical applications.

accessibility.reading_level: Teen discussion with technical terms defined and claims tested against context.
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Use precise language; define specialist terms and separate evidence from conclusion.
neurodiversity_supports: Allow written rather than spoken responses.
sensory_notes: No required role-play, public disclosure, or competitive performance.
non_reader_support: Provide concise claim cards or summaries without replacing the biblical text.

do_not_ask: Do not ask students to rank people by worth, intelligence, disability, sex, ethnicity, or productivity.
Do not require students to defend a family’s creation view publicly.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Correct demeaning claims immediately, protect students from public identity debates, and keep model disagreement non-salvific.
